This miscellaneous appeal having been heard and re
 orders, coming on for pronouncement this day, Justice Achal K
 Paliwal pronounced the following
 Order

This appeal by the claimants under section 173(1) of the Motor Vehicles Act is arising out of the award dated 06.01.2022 passed by 27th Member MACT, Indore in Claim Case No.1492/2019 seeking enhancement of compensation amount awarded by the Tribunal.
2. The date of accident, negligence and the issue of liability are not in dispute and the findings recorded by the Tribunal in this regard are also not in question.

As per the findings of the Tribunal,
for the death of Manish Bamotriya, the Tribunal has awarded a total compensation of Rs.17,75,942/-
along with interest.

The breakup of the compensation amount is as under:
Income of deceased 6,500/-+40%(F.P.)with  deduction with multiplier of 18 =
Rs.14,74,200/-

2  Consortium and Love and affection Rs. 40,000x3 (+
 to parents =Rs,1,64,000/-
 Loss of estate Rs.16,500  Funeral expenses Rs.16,500/-
 Medical Bills Rs.1,04,742/-
 Total Amount Rs.17,75,942/- + 7% interes 3.

Learned counsel for the appellants submits that the Tribunal has committed an error in not awarding just and proper amount of compensation in the case as the amount awarded by the Tribunal is on the lower side.
The Tribunal has erred in assessing the income of the deceased as he used to earn Rs.25,000/- from his milk business and electrician work.
Looking to the age, occupation, date of accident and the earning of the deceased prevalent on the date of accident, the income of the deceased deserves to be enhanced.
The amount awarded under other heads such as consortium, love and affection are also on the lower side, hence, prays for just and proper amount of compensation in the case.

4. On the other hand, learned counsel for the Insurance Company argued in support of the impugned award and contended that the Claims Tribunal has rightly awarded the compensation amount in the case which does not call for any interference by this Court.
5. After hearing learned counsel for the parties and going through the record, I find substance in the arguments advanced by the counsel for the appellants.

Considering the facts and circumstances of the case, arguments made by the counsel for the appellants and the evidence that came on record, in the considered opinion of this Court, the compensation awarded by the Tribunal deserves to be enhanced as under:
Income of deceased 7,375/-+40%(F.P.) with  deduction with multiplier of 18 =
Rs.16,72,750/-
Consortium and Love and affection Rs. 44,000x4 =1,76,000/-
 to parents  Loss of estate Rs.16,500  Funeral expenses Rs.16,500/-

Medical Bills Rs.1,04,742/-
 Total Amount Rs.19,86,492 with interest 6.
Thus, the just and proper amount of compensation in the instant case is Rs.19,86,492/- as against the award of the Tribunal of Rs.17,75,942/-.
Accordingly, the appellants are entitled to an additional sum of Rs.2,10,550/- over and above the amount which has been awarded by the Tribunal.
